masteryZone.q: Which Buddhist symbol represents Gautama Buddha's Enlightenment?
masteryZone.sol: The Bodhi Tree (Peepal tree) represents the enlightenment (Nirvana) attained by Siddhartha at Bodh Gaya.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Siddhartha Gautama's mother died shortly after his birth, and he was raised by Gautami.
masteryZone.sol: Queen Mahamaya died seven days after Siddhartha's birth, and he was raised by his stepmother, Mahapajapati Gotami.

masteryZone.q: The Eightfold Path is grouped into which three categories?
masteryZone.sol: Ashtangika Marga is categorized into Pragna (Wisdom), Sheela (Conduct), and Samadhi (Meditation).

masteryZone.q: The doctrine stating there is no permanent eternal soul in Buddhism is called ________.
masteryZone.sol: Anatta (or Anatman) is the core doctrine of non-self or no permanent soul.

masteryZone.q: Which Pitaka includes the Kathavatthu, containing debates on sectarian views?
masteryZone.sol: The Kathavatthu is a part of the Abhidhamma Pitaka, compiled during the Third Council.

masteryZone.q: In which language was the early Buddhist canon composed?
During which Buddhist Council did the formal split into Hinayana and Mahayana take place?
masteryZone.sol: The Fourth Buddhist Council at Kashmir (72 AD) marks the formal split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Second Council was at Vaishali under Kalasoka. The Third Council was at Pataliputra under Ashoka.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following schools is associated with Tantric Buddhism and magical spells?
masteryZone.sol: Vajrayana (Tantric) Buddhism emerged around the 8th century AD, incorporating magical spells and rituals.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The destruction of Nalanda University contributed to the decline of Buddhism in India.
masteryZone.sol: True. The destruction of Nalanda by Turkic invaders led by Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late 12th century dealt a severe blow to Buddhist learning in India.
